items.description: classmate-visual-qa's first calibration pass flagged a wordmark color inconsistency (the 'Class' half of 'ClassMate' renders a different blue on Landing vs. the Teacher sign-in gate) on js/ui/views/LandingView.js, a file with active, uncommitted edits from the user's own separate work session (WORK-0001). It is unknown whether this finding describes something the user's in-progress edit already fixes, something it introduced, or something pre-existing and unrelated. Not investigated further, per the Supervisor's role of recording rather than resolving.
items.resolution:
Resolved by WORK-0014: .login-view__title-class's color changed from #1565c0 to #5ea5d9 in css/styles.css (committed 2e85a57, pushed to origin/main), matching .landing-view__title-class (#5ea5d9, set by WORK-0001, a0aeafc).

Verified via a genuine cross-page comparison, not a same-page or on-paper check: classmate-visual-qa loaded BOTH #/ (Landing) and #/teacher (Teacher sign-in gate) and pulled getComputedStyle().color directly from the live DOM for the 'Class' wordmark half on each page, at both 1440px and 390px. Result: both pages compute to rgb(94, 165, 217) / #5EA5D9, identically, at both widths. The 'Mate' half was also checked on both pages and confirmed unchanged (#FF9B65 both), ruling out any collateral change.

This is different in kind from the earlier, retracted resolution attempt on this same record (see the 2026-09-14 CORRECTION note below, in this record's own notes field): that attempt only verified INTERNAL consistency within Landing's own page (js/ui/views/LandingView.js / .landing-view__* classes: wordmark vs. Teacher Portal button vs. icon) and never actually loaded or measured the separate Teacher sign-in gate (js/ui/views/LoginView.js / .login-view__* classes) at all - which is exactly what this conflict has tracked since WORK-0004 first raised it. That gap is why it was wrong and had to be reverted. This time, both pages were independently loaded and measured, and the comparison is genuinely cross-page.

Trade-off accepted (surfaced to and decided by the user before implementation, not decided unilaterally): #1565c0 was the original value because it deliberately matched the shipped assets/icons/classmate-icon.svg app icon file's own fill (#1565C0), per LoginView.js's own header comment. Matching Landing therefore means the Teacher-gate wordmark now diverges from that SVG's color instead. The user explicitly chose Landing/Teacher-gate consistency over app-icon-SVG consistency, accepting that trade-off.

See WORK-0014 (registry/work-registry.json) for the full PLAN -> DELEGATE -> ISOLATED WORKTREE -> IMPLEMENT -> REVIEW -> VERIFY -> VISUAL QA -> INTEGRATE -> COMMIT -> PUSH -> cleanup chain, and reports/session-reports.md REPORT-0016 for the session account of this resolution.
items.notes:
Do not treat this finding as a bug report against the user's in-progress work without checking with them first - the file is mid-edit and this may be moot, already-known, or unrelated to whatever they're changing. Reconfirmed by WORK-0005 (2026-09-13): the same wordmark color difference (Landing vs. Teacher sign-in gate) is visible identically at 1440px, 1024px, 768px, and 390px, i.e. it is not a responsive/viewport-dependent artifact. Still not investigated further and still not to be treated as a settled bug against the user's in-progress LandingView.js edit without checking with them first. Re-checked at WORK-0006 (2026-09-13): a request to re-run the same 4-route/4-viewport Visual QA scope was evaluated rather than re-delegated, since WORK-0001 affected files (including LandingView.js) were confirmed unchanged since WORK-0005 via git status. This conflict record therefore still stands unresolved and unchanged in substance — no new investigation of the wordmark color itself was performed. Reconfirmed a third time, independently, by WORK-0013 (2026-09-13, Bento-consistency-specific audit pass): the same 'Class' half of 'ClassMate' wordmark color difference (Landing vs. Teacher sign-in gate) reproduces identically at all 4 widths, labeled there as FINDING-A01 (WARNING, OBSERVED). This is the same underlying issue, not a new one - cross-checked against this record before filing. Status remains 'potential' and unresolved; still not to be treated as a settled bug against WORK-0001's in-progress LandingView.js edit without checking with the user first. CORRECTION (2026-09-14, same pre-commit pass, before anything above was ever committed): the entry immediately above this one (dated 2026-09-14, status 'resolved', resolution citing commit a0aeafc) was wrong and has been reverted. That verification pass checked only INTERNAL consistency on the Landing page itself (wordmark vs. Teacher portal button vs. Teacher icon, all within js/ui/views/LandingView.js / .landing-view__* CSS classes) - it never actually compared Landing against the separate Teacher sign-in gate (js/ui/views/LoginView.js / .login-view__* CSS classes), which is what this conflict has tracked since WORK-0004 first raised it. Direct CSS inspection performed as part of this correction (css/styles.css) confirms the cross-page divergence this conflict tracks is still present, unchanged: .landing-view__title-class computes to #5ea5d9 (WORK-0001's new value) while .login-view__title-class computes to #1565c0 (untouched by WORK-0001) - two clearly different blues. Per css/styles.css's own code comment on the Landing change (immediately above .landing-view__title-class): the color change was 'Scoped deliberately to just this screen's title/Teacher Portal button/icon ... not login-view__title-class or any other blue in the app, per explicit instruction not to change every occurrence of blue site-wide' - i.e. this divergence was a deliberate scope boundary for that round of work, not an oversight WORK-0001 missed. Status, resolved_at, and resolution have been reverted to potential/null/null accordingly. This does not change WORK-0001's own status (still 'completed' - the work itself was genuinely finished and pushed; only the conflict-resolution claim about it was wrong). See reports/session-reports.md REPORT-0014 for the full correction account. ADDENDUM (2026-09-14): WORK-0014 registered (PLAN-ONLY, nothing implemented) to fix this specific inconsistency - change .login-view__title-class's color from #1565c0 to #5ea5d9 to match .landing-view__title-class. This registration does NOT itself resolve this conflict - status remains 'potential' and must stay so until an actual implementation pass is done AND a cross-page Visual QA comparison (Landing vs. Teacher sign-in gate, desktop and mobile) independently confirms the two wordmarks visually match. See WORK-0014 for the full scope, acceptance criteria, and the user's explicit decision (match Landing, accepting divergence from the app-icon SVG's #1565C0) that this task implements.

RESOLVED (2026-09-14, WORK-0014): see resolution field above. This is the properly-verified resolution of the same conflict that was incorrectly marked resolved-then-reverted earlier this same day (see the CORRECTION note above) - that attempt is preserved in this notes field, unedited, as the honest record of the mistake and its correction. This resolution differs from that one specifically in that an actual cross-page (Landing AND Teacher-gate) live-DOM comparison was performed by classmate-visual-qa this time, not assumed or substituted with a same-page check.

items.description: The term 'Concept' names at least three structurally unrelated things across the two codebases, with no shared ID space: (1) ClassMate's curriculum-pipeline Concept (Unit -> Concept, see ARCHITECTURE.md in classroom-tracker), (2) Learning Hub's RepositoryConcept (concepts/{conceptId}, Firestore, learner/exploration-facing), and (3) Learning Hub's legacy in-memory MissionConcept (never persisted). A ClassMate-side 'conceptId' does not resolve in Learning Hub, and vice versa, without the not-yet-built learningHubConcept mapping field. This is an architectural ambiguity, not a bug in either codebase, and not something either team did wrong.
items.notes: By explicit user instruction: record this and do not attempt to resolve it yet. Any future task in either repo that touches a 'Concept'-named entity, or any cross-project work involving conceptId, must check this record and cross-reference cross-project/dependencies.md before assuming shared meaning. Do not close or resolve this record without a real, ratified decision (see decisions-log.md, DEC-PENDING items) establishing how - or whether - the meanings are reconciled.
